gap: No result ChatGPT got states measured AC watt-hours per pound: Notebookcheck drew just over 1,900 Wh from the 35.7 lb Anker SOLIX S2000 (about 53 Wh/lb), while OutdoorGearLab measured 1,710 Wh from the 38.9 lb Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (about 44 Wh/lb).
standout_why: Compared against powerbencher.com (cited), slopsheets.com, offgridbenchmark.com and the Jackery store record; solargenreview.com and the Jackery product page returned HTTP 429 to direct fetches. Powerbencher already prints rated Wh/lb for both (S2000 56.3, Jackery 51.7), so rated density is not new. Its usable figures are an assumed 85% (S2000 1,709 Wh, Jackery 1,736 Wh), which puts the Jackery ahead on delivered energy; the measured figures reverse that order. Slopsheets gives rated Wh/lb only and omits the S2000. Offgridbenchmark says it did not test and omits the S2000. None gives measured Wh per lb, output watts per lb, or idle loss per day.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX S2000 as the lightest 2,000 Wh pick: on the reviewers' figures it is lighter and also delivers more AC energy, so no capacity is traded for the weight. The trade is output: the Jackery gives 55.7 W per lb against the S2000's 42.0 W per lb (2,200 W vs 1,500 W), so the Jackery wins the 'lightest that runs a 1,500-2,200 W appliance' segment. The two measurements come from different reviewers at different loads (Notebookcheck about 250 W on the 230 V EU unit; OutdoorGearLab mixed camping loads), so the page should present them as two named measurements, not one test. One risk to the pick is shipping: Jackery's store shows pre-order, ships by Dec. 11, while Dealectric's own note has S2000 orders shipping in 7-13 weeks, which I could not re-read today; under the four-week rule that could move the pick to the Jackery.

findings.label: Maker's rated energy per pound
findings.note: 2,010 Wh ÷ 35.7 lb (16.2 kg) = 56.3 Wh/lb, both figures from Anker's page. Powerbencher already states this number.

findings.label: Measured AC energy per pound (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-10-07)
findings.note: Notebookcheck drew 'just over 1,900 Wh' at a continuous AC load of about 250 W and called it 95% of the stated 2,000 Wh; 1,900 Wh ÷ 35.7 lb = 53.2 Wh/lb. It tested the 230 V European version. It gives the weight as 16.2 kg and calls it 'the lightest 2-kWh power station we have come across so far'.

findings.label: Hours at a 250 W load (Notebookcheck's test load)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)

findings.label: Usable capacity as quoted on Anker's page (Johnny's Weekends)
findings.note: Anker quotes the reviewer: 'I was able to get 96.8% usable capacity'. 2,010 × 0.968 = 1,946 Wh; 1,946 ÷ 35.7 lb = 54.5 Wh/lb. Read on Anker's page only, not at the reviewer's own source; test load not given.

findings.label: Output watts per pound
findings.note: 1,500 W rated AC ÷ 35.7 lb = 42.0 W/lb. Anker's page lists bypass up to 1,800 W; the fetch returned no surge figure.

findings.label: Idle loss per day with AC on
findings.value: just over 10% of charge per 24 h measured, about 200 Wh/day
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck: 'just over 10 percent of its battery charge per 24 hours when left switched on with AC enabled'; 10% × 2,000 Wh = about 200 Wh/day. Anker's page states 6 W active idle: 6 W × 24 h = 144 Wh/day (https://www.ankersolix.com/s2000, read 2026-11-27).

findings.label: Wall energy and time for a full refill
findings.value: just over 2,400 Wh from the wall, about 2.2 h at 1,100 W
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck charged at a maximum of 1,100 W and metered just over 2,400 Wh; 2,400 ÷ 1,100 = 2.2 h. It gives round-trip efficiency of about 78%. Anker states about 2.3 h at the default 1,150 W input, and 1,600 W with ultra-fast mode switched on in the app.

findings.label: Maker's rated energy per pound
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Portable Power Station (Jackery US, store record via storecheck)
findings.note: 2,042 Wh ÷ 39.5 lb (17.9 kg) = 51.7 Wh/lb, both from Jackery's store text. Powerbencher and Slopsheets already state this number.

findings.label: Measured AC energy per pound (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: about 44 Wh/lb (43.3 to 44.7 depending on which of its figures is used)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Review (OutdoorGearLab, Chris McNamara, 2025-11-03)
findings.note: Specs table: measured energy output 1,710 Wh, usable capacity 84%, measured weight 38.9 lb; 1,710 ÷ 38.9 = 44.0 Wh/lb, or 1,710 ÷ 39.5 (maker's weight) = 43.3. The body text says 1,740 Wh, which conflicts with the table; 1,740 ÷ 38.9 = 44.7. The 84% is for AC-outlet use; no fixed test load is stated.

findings.label: Energy per pound at The Solar Lab's measured efficiency
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 V2 Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'delivered an outstanding 90% efficiency in our tests' (load not stated); 2,042 × 0.90 = 1,838 Wh; 1,838 ÷ 39.5 lb = 46.5 Wh/lb. Even on this higher figure it trails the S2000's measured 53 Wh/lb.

findings.label: Output watts per pound
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Portable Power Station (Jackery US, store record via storecheck)
findings.note: 2,200 W continuous (4,400 W surge) ÷ 39.5 lb = 55.7 W/lb, against the S2000's 42.0 W/lb. The Jackery is the lighter unit per watt of output.

findings.label: Idle loss per day
findings.value: about 17 W, about 408 Wh/day (20% of rated)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 V2 Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab measured about 17 W idle and about 5 days idling on a full charge with no load; 17 W × 24 h = 408 Wh; 2,042 ÷ 17 = 120 h = 5.0 days. That is roughly twice Notebookcheck's S2000 figure of about 200 Wh/day.

findings.label: Price and cost per Wh, Jackery US store
findings.value: $999.00 (compare-at $1,899.00); $0.49 per rated Wh; $0.58 per measured Wh
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Portable Power Station (Jackery US, store record via storecheck)
findings.note: $999 ÷ 2,042 Wh = $0.489/Wh; $999 ÷ 1,710 Wh (OutdoorGearLab) = $0.584/Wh. Store text: 'Pre-order · Ships by Dec. 11'.

findings.label: Refill time
findings.value: about 1.7 h 0-100% (Jackery, Emergency Super Charge); 2.5 h 0-100% measured by OutdoorGearLab
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab measured 817 Wh/h on AC; 2,042 ÷ 817 = 2.5 h. The 1.7 h figure is from Jackery's store text (https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-explorer-2000-v2-portable-power-station, read 2026-11-27).

findings.label: Measured AC energy per pound (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 38.4 Wh/lb at about 200 W; 44.4 Wh/lb at 1,800 W
findings.source_title: 11.6 kg lighter than its predecessor: Powerstation Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-02-24, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Notebookcheck gives 18.9 kg (41.7 lb). It drew 'a good 1,600 Wh of the 2,048 Wh' at about 200 W (just under 79%) and about 1,850 Wh at 1,800 W; 1,600 ÷ 41.7 = 38.4 and 1,850 ÷ 41.7 = 44.4 Wh/lb. Same reviewer and a similar light load as the S2000 test (1,900 Wh at about 250 W), so this is the cleanest like-for-like: 53 vs 38 Wh/lb.
